notice.title: Legal notice
notice.intro: This notice identifies the operator of Soma at somarecovery.app. It does not describe a commercial company.
notice.identityBody:
Soma is offered by a natural person resident in Spain. It does not claim that a company exists.

Identification: [NOMBRE DEL RESPONSABLE]. [NIF / identity document, if published]. [DOMICILIO A EFECTOS LEGALES]. A postal address is not published unless it is configured.
notice.contactBody:
Contact email: [CORREO DE CONTACTO]. Telephone: [TELÉFONO, if published]. Data protection officer: [DELEGADO DE PROTECCIÓN DE DATOS, if applicable; otherwise “not appointed”].

That email is the intended channel for exercising rights and for communications about these documents.
notice.siteBody: The public site of the service is https://somarecovery.app. The web interface and the API are hosted on Render.
notice.natureBody: Soma is an educational and motivational application about abstinence and recovery. It lets people explore catalog content and, if they later consent, personal tracking. It is not a healthcare provider, does not deliver clinical care, and is not a medical device. The beta is public and free. It includes no advertising, subscriptions, donations or monetisation.
notice.ipBody: The texts, illustrations, visible marks, educational catalogs and interface belong to their owner or to whoever the law provides. Personal use of the service does not authorise copying, extracting, reselling or systematically reusing that content. This text does not list specific third-party licences or assignments.
notice.relatedBody: Use of Soma is also described in the Terms of use, the Privacy policy and the Cookies and local storage information. Sign-up records that the person marked having read the terms and privacy and declared being 18 or over. That does not imply consent for special-category data.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes personal-data processing in Soma (somarecovery.app) according to the product inventory. There is no advertising, subscriptions, donations or sale of personal data. The beta is public, free and aimed at people aged 18 or over. Registration is open to people who meet that age.
privacy.knownTitle: What is confirmed and what is not
privacy.knownBody:
Confirmed: the controller is a natural person resident in Spain; the intended legal setting is the GDPR and Spain’s LOPDGDD; the beta is aimed at people aged 18 or over; consent for substance, abstinence and journal data is contextual and is not part of registration; the website and API are hosted on Render; the PostgreSQL database is hosted on Supabase; encrypted backups are stored on Cloudflare R2 via GitHub Actions.

Controller identification: [NOMBRE DEL RESPONSABLE]. Contact: [CORREO DE CONTACTO]. [DOMICILIO A EFECTOS LEGALES].

The repository does not document each provider’s region or contractual clauses for international transfers. Retention of logs at Render, GitHub and the email provider, if used, follows those providers.
privacy.identityBody:
The controller is a natural person. Identification: [NOMBRE DEL RESPONSABLE]. [NIF / identity document, if published]. [DOMICILIO A EFECTOS LEGALES]. Contact: [CORREO DE CONTACTO].

A postal address is not published unless it is configured. The email is the contact channel for these policies.
privacy.purposeBody:
Soma processes data to: create and maintain an account; authenticate access and keep a session; show educational content; if consent is given, store personal tracking of substances, abstinence and the journal and calculate derived estimates, achievements and XP; allow educational missions; receive optional product feedback; send password-reset email when that sending is enabled; keep database backups; and allow account deletion or withdrawal of consent.

Data are not used for advertising or to commercialise profiles.
privacy.basesBody:
This section describes how the product’s behaviour maps onto GDPR Articles 6 and 9. It is not a legal opinion.

Performance of the service (Article 6.1.b): account data (email, password stored as a hash, display name), authentication and session, password reset, educational missions and their associated XP, and profile fields used by the catalog’s educational estimates (biological sex, birth year and optional weight). Those profile fields are not gated on special-category consent.

Explicit consent (Articles 6.1.a and 9.2.a): processing of information about substances, abstinence, the wellbeing journal, personal milestones, recovery achievements and XP from those sources. That consent is not requested at registration. It is requested later, specifically, unticked by default and separately, when the person first wants to store those data (for example during tracking onboarding, in the journal, or from Account).

Sending feedback is voluntary and is used to improve the product. The product also deletes it when special-category consent is withdrawn, because it treats it as linked to the person’s path. No separate legal basis is recorded for that message.

The technical session cookie is used to keep authenticated access. No other basis is asserted here beyond what is needed to provide that access.

This text does not invoke legitimate interests under Article 6.1.f or other bases not observed in the product.
privacy.dataBody:
Account: email address, password stored as a hash, display name, biological sex, birth year, optional weight, and onboarding status. Email and password are required for the account. Name and sex are requested at sign-up. Weight is optional.

At sign-up the person enters a date of birth. That date is used to check that they have already turned 18; only the year is stored on the account. No identity document is requested.

Sign-up also stores, on an append-only basis and without an IP address, that the person ticked the terms of use, privacy and adult-age boxes (purpose, document version and date).

Password reset, when email sending is enabled, uses the account email address.
privacy.specialBody:
If the person consents, Soma may store chosen substances, year started, frequency, last-use date, status (for example abstinence), journal entries (text, mood, sleep, energy, anxiety, craving and wellbeing scales, tags) and personal milestones. That information may be health data or another special category under GDPR Article 9.

Consent is explicit and contextual: there is no health checkbox at registration. Without that permission the product does not write those data. Tracking onboarding can be skipped and educational content and the demo remain available.

Withdrawal is done from Account, with a password. It deletes those data from the live database and the derived data the product treats as linked to them (recovery achievements, feedback and XP from sensitive sources). It does not close the account and does not restore deleted data if consent is granted again later. The history of grants and withdrawals is kept as evidence of the action (purpose, version and date; no IP).

A new consent does not restore deleted data.
privacy.derivedBody:
Educational missions record the completed mission, content version and date. Completing a mission does not require special-category consent. That record and mission XP remain if consent is withdrawn.

Recovery achievements and XP from the journal, milestones, tracking onboarding or achievements are tied to consent. They are deleted from the live database on withdrawal.

Levels and titles are calculated from total XP. After a withdrawal, the total is realigned with what remains (for example mission XP).
privacy.authBody:
Authentication is first-party (an access JWT in browser memory and the HttpOnly cookie soma_refresh). There is no external identity provider such as Auth0.

A session may store: refresh-token hash, session family identifier, expiry, a truncated user-agent, and, if recorded, a hash of a network identifier, not the raw IP address.

The password is not stored in clear text.
privacy.feedbackBody:
A person may optionally send a product message (category, title and body). The service does not email that text to the team from the API. A fingerprint (hash) is stored to limit duplicates. Sending feedback does not grant XP.

That record is deleted when special-category consent is withdrawn and when the account is deleted. Journal export does not include feedback.
privacy.processorsBody:
The web interface and the API are hosted on Render. The PostgreSQL database (Prisma) is hosted on Supabase. Backups are encrypted with age and sent to a Cloudflare R2 bucket by GitHub Actions on the main branch.

If password-reset email is enabled, the product can send it through Resend (api.resend.com). If that sending is disabled, no reset email is sent.

Authentication is first-party. This text does not claim that processor contracts are signed, nor a full list of sub-processors, nor each provider’s region.
privacy.transfersBody:
Hosting location and an international transfer are not the same thing. A service may be deployed in a given region and still involve processing or access from outside that region or the European Economic Area.

Render hosts the web interface and the API. The confirmed hosting location for the API is Frankfurt, Germany, in the European Economic Area.

Supabase hosts the PostgreSQL database. The confirmed hosting location is the United Kingdom. The United Kingdom is covered by an adequacy decision of the European Commission. While that decision remains in force, a transfer of personal data from the European Economic Area to the United Kingdom does not, by that fact alone, require additional standard contractual clauses.

Cloudflare R2 stores the encrypted backups. WEUR (Western Europe) is the bucket’s configured location. That setting indicates an intended geographical location; it does not promise exclusive residence of the data in the European Economic Area and is not the same as a jurisdictional residency restriction.

Resend sends password-recovery emails. According to its public documentation, it stores service data in the United States.

These providers publish data-processing addenda. Those documents set out safeguards for transfers outside the European Economic Area where no adequacy decision applies, including the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses. This section describes the content of those public documents. It does not state that the controller has executed, accepted or downloaded the relevant addendum for the Soma account, nor that a particular certification or privacy framework applies to that account.
privacy.retentionBody:
While the account exists, product data (account, profile and, if consent is given, tracking) are kept in the live database. There is no inactivity expiry in the code.

If the person deletes the account, Soma deletes the user in the live database and, by cascade, associated product data, including sessions. If they only withdraw special-category consent, the deletion described in that section applies; the account and educational missions remain.

Encrypted backups in Cloudflare R2 follow an operational cycle separate from live-database retention: daily copies kept for 7 days and weekly copies kept for 28 days. That cycle describes how long an encrypted dump is stored; it is not a maximum retention period for personal data in the service. A dump taken before an erasure or a withdrawal may remain until that copy expires.

Password-reset tokens expire after 30 minutes, unless the service is configured otherwise. The refresh cookie lasts 14 days by default (AUTH_REFRESH_EXPIRES_DAYS), unless the service is configured otherwise. Logs at Render, GitHub and, if used, Resend follow those providers’ periods, which are not set in Soma’s code.
privacy.cookiesBody: Details are in the Cookies and local storage information. In short: the technical cookie soma_refresh for the session; interface preferences in the browser’s local storage; the landing intro in sessionStorage; the access JWT is not persisted. No advertising cookies or third-party analytics cookies have been identified.
privacy.advertisingBody: There is no advertising, subscriptions, donations or paid features. Soma does not sell or commercialise personal data.
privacy.ageBody: The beta is aimed at people aged 18 or over. Sign-up requires an unticked adult-age declaration and a date of birth. The server checks that this date means 18 years have already been completed on the civil date in Europe/Madrid. Only the year is kept on the account. Soma does not ask for an identity document: a minor could declare a false date. That limit is also described in the terms of use.
privacy.rightsBody:
You may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing that produces legal effects, and, where applicable, portability, under GDPR Articles 15 to 22 and the LOPDGDD.

The product today provides: viewing profile and tracking data; editing profile (name, sex, birth year, weight) and editing usages and journal entries when consent is active; journal export (entries and personal milestones, not a complete export of all data); withdrawal of special-category consent; and password-confirmed account deletion.

The account email cannot be changed from Account. There is no single download of every datum. There is no specific restriction or objection flow beyond the contact email and withdrawal or deletion.

For rights not covered by those screens: [CORREO DE CONTACTO]. The product does not publish an internal procedure for deadlines or identity checks. That channel alone is not a complete rights procedure.

You may lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD), www.aepd.es.
privacy.deletionBody:
Account deletion removes the profile and product data in the live database and invalidates sessions. It does not immediately erase backups or provider logs. Encrypted copies in R2 follow their 7-day and 28-day cycle. No deadline is stated for total disappearance outside that operational cycle.

Withdrawing consent does not delete the account and does not instantly erase backups.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms govern the use of Soma (somarecovery.app) in the public beta.
terms.natureBody: Soma is an educational and motivational companion about abstinence and recovery. It offers a catalog of content (organs, curves, phases, neurotransmitters, missions and achievements) and, if the person consents, personal tracking. It is not a clinical service.
terms.betaBody: Access is public and free, with no advertising, subscriptions, donations or payments. There is no predetermined end date for the beta. Registration is open to people aged 18 or over.
terms.ageBody: Soma is aimed at people aged 18 or over. Sign-up requires declaring that age (an unticked checkbox) and a date of birth with which the server checks that 18 years have already been completed, so a minor born in the same calendar year is not accepted automatically. Soma does not ask for ID and does not verify the declaration with documents: someone who enters a false date could bypass the check. The year is stored on the account; the day and month are not kept.
terms.accountsBody: The account is personal. The holder must keep their credentials and must not enter other people’s data. The account email cannot be changed from the Account screen. Sign-up requires ticking that the person has read these terms and the privacy policy, and declaring adult age. That does not imply health-data consent.
terms.useBody: The service is offered for personal, educational and motivational use. It must not be used to diagnose, treat or monitor other people, or to extract, copy or resell the catalog. People who use Soma are responsible for how they interpret the information. This text does not attempt an absolute exclusion of liability or waivers of rights that cannot legally be waived.
terms.educationBody: The catalog shows modelled physiological estimates, recovery curves, neurotransmitter information, abstinence phases, educational advice and an anatomy explorer. These are published contents for understanding general models. They do not measure the person’s body.
terms.modesBody: The demo (/preview) lets people explore the interface and catalog without an account and without storing a personal path. Live tracking, when there is an account and consent, applies the same educational formulas to the dates and data the person records. DEMO and LIVE are not a clinical measurement. Without consent, live tracking does not store substances or journal entries.
terms.estimatesBody: Curves, “progress” percentages, phases and neurotransmitter models are illustrative. They do not predict individual recovery, do not calibrate a real physiological state and do not replace a health professional’s judgement. Achievements unlock when an educational catalog trajectory crosses a threshold; they do not prove that an organ has recovered.
terms.medicalBody: Soma does not diagnose, prescribe, clinically monitor or provide individualized medical treatment. It is not a medical device.
terms.emergencyBody: If there is an emergency, self-harm ideation, intoxication or any situation that needs assistance, contact emergency services or a health professional, not Soma. Soma is not a crisis channel and not a substitute for medical, psychological or social care.
terms.availabilityBody: The service is offered as a beta. There may be interruptions, errors or incomplete features. Permanent availability and a recovery outcome are not promised.
terms.changesBody: Soma may change educational features or these texts during the beta. If a change is material for people who already have an account, they will be informed in an appropriate way (for example in the service or via the contact email). No specific notice period is set here.
terms.deletionBody: The account holder may delete the account from the application, confirming with their password. The effect on the live database and on backups is described in the privacy policy. Withdrawing special-category consent is not the same as deleting the account.
terms.advertisingBody: There is no advertising, payments, subscriptions or donations under these terms.
terms.contactBody: Contact: [CORREO DE CONTACTO]. The operator is a natural person resident in Spain. Identification: [NOMBRE DEL RESPONSABLE], [DOMICILIO A EFECTOS LEGALES]. This text does not set governing law or venue. Intended setting: Spain and European law.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage information
cookies.intro: This text documents only what has been observed in the product. It does not describe analytics or advertising tools that have not been identified.
cookies.scopeBody: Soma uses a first-party technical cookie for the authenticated session and several browser storage values for interface preferences. The access JWT is kept in memory, not in persistent storage. No IndexedDB or service worker that persists data has been identified.
cookies.cookieBody:
Name: soma_refresh. First-party. HttpOnly, path /auth. Purpose: refresh the authentication session. It is necessary to stay signed in without re-entering the password on every request. Duration: 14 days by default (AUTH_REFRESH_EXPIRES_DAYS), unless the service is configured otherwise. No advertising third party is involved. SameSite: lax in the usual case; the code may use none and Secure if a cross-origin scenario is configured.

It is not an advertising or audience-measurement cookie.
cookies.localBody:
These values are stored in localStorage on the same origin until the person deletes them or clears browser storage. They are not required for authentication. They remember interface preferences:

soma.i18n.lang: interface language (Spanish or English).

soma.shell.sidebarCollapsed: whether the sidebar is collapsed.

soma.onb01.{user identifier}: onboarding tutorial state.

soma.achievements.celebrate.sound: sound preference when celebrating an achievement.

On sign-in the client deletes the legacy key soma.auth.token if it exists; that key is no longer used to store the session.
cookies.sessionBody: soma.landing-v2.intro.seen is stored in sessionStorage so the landing intro is not repeated during the same browser session. It is cleared when the tab or browser is closed, according to ordinary sessionStorage behaviour. No third party is involved.
cookies.memoryBody: The access JWT stays in memory for as long as the authenticated tab lasts. It is not documented as a cookie or as local storage.
cookies.thirdBody: The code has not been found to contain advertising pixels, third-party analytics tags, or non-essential tracking tools. Infrastructure providers (hosting, database, email, backups) are described in the privacy policy; they do not inject marketing cookies into the interface according to the current inventory.
cookies.bannerBody: The technologies described are first-party and, for soma_refresh, necessary for authenticated access. The others are interface preferences. This text does not introduce a cookie-consent banner because no advertising, analytics or non-essential tracking technology that would require one has been identified. If such a technology were added later, this information would need to be reviewed.
